meaning: The number 22 symbolizes completeness and wholeness, linked to the 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet.
description: In Jewish tradition, there are 22 letters in the Hebrew alphabet, regarded as the building blocks God used to create the world. Psalm 119, the longest psalm in the Bible, is structured into 22 sections—one for each Hebrew letter—emphasizing completeness in God's word. The number 22 is therefore associated with revelation, creative power, and divine order, representing a wholeness where all elements of God's plan are present.

versions.reason: [minor] The description contains an interesting detail about the 22 generations from Adam to Jacob that works better as a footnote, since it interrupts the main text's flow regarding the alphabet/creation theme. In addition, footnotes are completely missing, and it is good practice to move such specific traditional details there.; [minor] A footnote could be added about the kabbalistic tradition concerning the 22 letters as the building blocks of creation, since this originates from Sefer Yetzirah (Book of Creation), an important kabbalistic/early mystical text. Mentioning the source strengthens credibility.; [minor] The claim about 22 generations from Adam to Jacob should be clarified. According to Genesis, it is actually common to count these as 22 generations (Adam, Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah, Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor, Terah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob = 22), but this is best known from rabbinic tradition and fits better as a footnote.

footnotes.text: The concept of the 22 Hebrew letters as the building blocks of creation is described in detail in Sefer Yetzirah (Book of Creation), an early Jewish mystical text from the first centuries CE. It describes how God combined the 22 letters to form all that has been created.
According to rabbinic tradition, there are 22 generations from Adam to Jacob (Israel), marking a completed cycle in salvation history—from the first human to the patriarch of Israel's twelve tribes.
Psalm 119 is an acrostic poem where each section of eight verses begins with a specific Hebrew letter in alphabetical order. This form emphasizes that God's law is complete and all-encompassing.
